payload.prompt:
You are reviewing an Algebra 2 lesson packet just drafted for an upcoming observation day on Friday 2026-05-15. Your job is to STEELMAN the design — defend each choice against all constraints, then identify what could STILL go wrong, and suggest specific fixes.

CONTEXT
=======
- Lesson: 4-3 (Multiply and Divide Rational Expressions), Period 1.
- Observation day = Friday 5/15, single 65-min period (Period F).
- Class context: ELL-heavy, <=10 students, solo teacher, no aide.
- Visual + structural reference: L35_P3_obs_student.docx (repo root) — the admin-supplied "DOCX format" that the new packet must mirror in spirit and visually.
- Format we adopted: 4 problems matching the DOCX exactly:
  1. Do Now (Explore & Reason — conceptual gateway, DOK-2)
  2. Apply – Make Sense and Persevere (multi-step DOK-2)
  3. Performance Task (DOK-3 spine)
  4. Exit Ticket (short conceptual prompt + 2 reflection prompts)

DRAFT TO REVIEW
===============
File: tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex (4 pages, one section per page, white-space-as-writing-room — no underline rules visible to students).

Problem map (every student-facing item must trace to Savvas bank — hard rule):
- Do Now: Savvas Model & Discuss "Explore & Reason" — graph of y=x+2 with parts A (domain) / B (sketch with x!=2 excluded) / C (Use Structure — "what kind of function might have a graph like this?"). Bridges into rational functions.
- Apply: Savvas Practice #35 — cylinder A vs B V/SA ratio comparison. Savvas labels DOK-1; Klimsara/Colson argue DOK-2 (multi-step modeling + comparison).
- Performance Task (DOK-3 SPINE): Savvas Practice #36 — Lupe carnival probability. Savvas labels DOK-2 (Model with Mathematics); Klimsara argues DOK-3 because students must build the rational expression from geometry, simplify, state restrictions, and interpret as probability. Scaffolded into A (build) / B (simplify + domain in physical context) / C (evaluate at x=4 + judge fairness).
- Exit Ticket: Savvas Practice #13 — Higher Order Thinking, "Why are rational expressions closed under x and div?" (Savvas-declared DOK-3). Plus 3 sentence frames, plus 2 reflection prompts ("What did you learn?" / "What did you like?").

Throughline (the spine the four problems collectively express):
"Domain restriction is the soul of a rational expression — it survives even when factors cancel."

CONSTRAINTS TO CHECK (from CLAUDE.md "Hard rules" + "Klimsara-adapted 3-period cadence" sections)
==================================================================================================
1. Savvas-only: Every student-facing problem traces to a Savvas bank ID in questionbank/registry.jsonl. Cross-check the 4 problems against Savvas SE/TE (a2_4-3_SE.tex / a2_4-3_TE.tex).
2. Single-DOK3 spine per period: The packet has exactly ONE DOK-3 spine. Identify which problem is the spine and verify the labeling.
3. Summary exit, not CER: Exit Ticket is a recap + reflection, NOT full claim-evidence-reasoning writing in 5 min.
4. Try-Its in-class as TPS only: N/A here (no Try-Its on this packet).
5. Klimsara framework phases respected: Do Now <=10, Launch 10-15, Explore 35-40, Share/Summary 5-15, Exit. The 4-problem DOCX format implicitly collapses Launch into Apply — confirm timing math still works for a 65-min period.
6. ELL support: sentence frames present where students must speak or write longer-form.
7. No answer leaks: student-facing prompts keep symbolic form (no computed answers substituted in).
8. Visual/structural mirror to L35_P3_obs DOCX: title centered, 3-row objectives table at top, plain bold section heads, 4 problems in same order, reflection prompts in Exit, Name line before Exit.
9. Single-page-per-section flow: 4 pages total, Exit Ticket on the last page.

REFERENCE FILES (read as needed — paths relative to the working dir)
====================================================================
- CLAUDE.md (hard rules, Klimsara cadence, class context, assessment coverage)
- tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex (the draft you are reviewing)
- a2_4-3_SE.tex (Savvas Student Edition for 4-3 — ground truth for problem statements, 544 lines)
- a2_4-3_TE.tex (Savvas Teacher Edition for 4-3 — DOK labels, teaching notes, 1117 lines)
- 4-3_klimsara/envAlg2_04_03_LessonPacket.tex (Klimsara's reference packet for 4-3)
- 4-3_colson/a2_4-3_problems.tex (problem set we drew from — this is where #13/#35/#36/#40 + Explore-and-Reason TikZ live)
- 4-3_colson/a2_4-3_examples.tex (Examples 1-6 with worked solutions)
- tagging/4-3_pilot.jsonl (DAG tags for 4-3 items including prereq_ids, rehearses, skill_tokens, role)
- legacy/tex/L35_P3_obs_student.tex (the previous OBS-day packet, kept for style/format reference even though L43 mirrors the DOCX, not this older tex)
- tex/preamble.sty (shared LaTeX style — for context only; this packet doesn't import it)

DELIVER (sections in this order)
================================
Section A — STEELMAN (defend each design choice):
For each of the 4 problems, articulate WHY it was the right pick, citing specific constraints from CLAUDE.md and evidence from the Savvas TE/SE. 1-2 short paragraphs per problem.

Section B — RISKS (what could still go wrong):
3-7 specific risks. Each risk should cite a line number in tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex if applicable. Categories worth checking: timing miscalculation, DOK miscalibration, ELL inaccessibility, answer leak, visual/structural drift from DOCX, missing assessment alignment, prompt ambiguity, scaffolding mismatch, prerequisite gap.

Section C — FIXES (specific, actionable):
For each risk in Section B, propose a specific fix. Include the exact LaTeX change (find/replace text or short paragraph rewrite) where possible.

Section D — VERDICT:
One of: "Ship it as-is" / "Ship after fixing X, Y, Z" / "Hold — fundamental problem with W." One short paragraph of justification.

Be terse. Be specific. Cite file:line whenever you can. Do not write or edit any files — this is a read-only review.
